source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961} in the morning{H1242}, all the chief{H1419} sages{H2450} and the elders{H6931} took{H3947} counsel{H6098} against{H5048} Yeshua{H3442}, that they should surely kill him{H2026}.

greek_deviations: 'The chief SAGES (חכמים) and the ancients' — Greek Matthew has 'the chief priests and elders of the people.' The Hebrew names the learned class by its rabbinic title.
translation_notes: מכל וכל — 'from every possible way, surely' (the transcription's footnote 169), a living-Hebrew idiom of totality.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק קי״ב (Perek 112) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (27:1): החכמים] הכהנים A.

verses.translation: And bound{H7194}, they led him{H1980} to the house{H1004} of Pontius Pilat, who was the official{H1489}.

translation_notes: גזבר (H1489, gizbar) — 'treasurer,' the Persian-loan administrative title of Ezra 1:8. The Hebrew gives Pilate a Persian-period Hebrew office-name where Greek has ἡγεμών ('governor'); Howard renders 'commander.'
פו״טץ פילא״ט — the foreign name doubly marked with the scribal gershayim, as the text marks all loanwords.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:2): פו״טץ] פונץ AB, פריץ EF, פוטס G.

verses.translation: And then{H227}, when Yudah{H3063} Iskeriota saw{H7200} that he was condemned{H1777}, he began{H2490} to return{H7725} in repentance{H8666}, and returned{H2350} the thirty{H7970} dinars to the chief{H1419} of the priests{H3548} and to the elders{H2205} of the people{H5971}.

one_way_hebrew: לשוב בתשובה — 'to turn in TESHUVAH': the Hebrew gives Judas the full vocabulary of repentance — שוב, the prophets' turning-word (Hos 14:2), doubled with its noun תשובה, the rabbinic term for repentance itself. Greek μεταμεληθείς ('feeling regret') is a weaker word, and the whole Christian-era debate over whether Judas 'truly repented' turns on a distinction the Hebrew text does not make.
translation_notes: דינרים — dinars (the Latin denarius as a Hebrew loanword); at 26:15 the sum was שלשים כסף, Zech 11:12's phrase; here the narrator uses the everyday coin-name.

verses.translation: He said{H559}: I have sinned{H2398}, for I have shed{H8210} innocent{H5355} blood{H1818}. And they said{H559} to him: What{H4100} is that to us? You will see{H7200} to it.

one_way_hebrew: דם נקי — 'innocent blood,' the Torah's fixed legal phrase, and Deut 27:25 is its exact application: 'Cursed be he that taketh a bribe to slay an innocent person (להכות נפש דם נקי).' Judas confesses himself under the Ebal curse — he took the bribe, the innocent blood is shed. The phrase runs through Deut 19:10-13 and 21:8-9 (the hand-washing rite Pilate will perform at v. 24). Greek αἷμα ἀθῷον translates the words; only the Hebrew reader stands on mount Ebal hearing them.

verses.translation: And he threw{H2236} the coins in the Sanctuary{H4720}, and went away{H1980}, and took{H3947} a rope{H2256} and hanged{H8518} himself{H6106}.

one_way_hebrew: וזרק המעות במקדש — the act performs Zech 11:13 before the narrator quotes it (v. 9): ואשליך אתו בית יהוה, 'and I cast them... in the house of YHWH.' The Hebrew reader watches the prophecy enacted, then hears it named.

ותלה עצמו — 'and HANGED himself' (תלה): the same verb the crowd will cry against his master (יתלוהו, v. 23) and by which the two thieves 'were hanged' (v. 38). One verb of hanging runs through the chapter — the betrayer, the betrayed, and the thieves — visible only in Hebrew, where Greek splits it into ἀπήγξατο and σταυρόω.

The scene is Ahithophel's: the trusted counselor who lifted his heel against David's anointed 'put his household in order and hanged himself' (2 Sam 17:23) — the only suicide-by-hanging in Scripture, and Ps 41:10's betrayer-at-the-table stands behind both.
translation_notes: מעות — the rabbinic word for coins (no biblical Strong's entry); the narrator's everyday Hebrew.

verses.translation: And the great ones{H1419} of the priests{H3548}, when they took{H3947} the coins, said{H559}: It is not fitting{H8505} that we put{H7760} these coins in the Sanctuary{H4720}, for they are the price{H1818} of blood{H1818}, given for the blood{H1818} of Yeshua{H3442}.

one_way_hebrew: שדמי דם הם — an untranslatable Hebrew pun: דמים means both 'money, price' and 'blood,' so 'they are דמי דם' says 'they are blood-money' with one word doing both duties, and בעד דמי יש״ו repeats it — 'for the blood(-price) of Yeshua.' Greek τιμὴ αἵματος ('price of blood') needs two different words and loses the wordplay that makes the priests' scruple sting.
translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads שלשים; the scan of Howard's text reads שנשים ('that we put'), corrected here.

verses.translation: And they took counsel{H3289} and gave{H5414} them for the field{H7704} of a man{H120}, a potter{H3335} of clay{H2789}, that the strangers{H1616} might be buried there{H8033}.
words: might prevail (so ms; sense: be buried)

one_way_hebrew: יוצר חרס — 'a potter of clay': the wording of Jer 19:1 (בקבק יוצר חרש, 'a potter's earthen flask') bought opposite the burial-field of Topheth (Jer 19:11, 'they shall bury in Topheth till there be no place to bury'). The Hebrew narrative touches Jeremiah's potter-and-burial oracle in its own words while naming ZECHARIAH for the silver-oracle (v. 9) — showing precisely how Greek Matthew's puzzling 'spoken by Jeremy the prophet' arose: two prophets stand behind the scene, and the Hebrew text keeps them straight.
translation_notes: שיגברו — so the base ms ('that the strangers might PREVAIL there' — evidently corrupt); mss ABG read שיקברו ('that they might BURY the strangers there'), which the sense requires and Howard's English follows: 'that they might (bury) strangers there.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:7): שיגברו] שיקברו ABG, שיגררו EF; ויועצו] ויתיעצו EF; אדם] של אדם F; חרס] omit EF.

verses.translation: And therefore{H3651} that field{H7704} is called{H7121} the Tent{H168} of Blood{H1818} until this day{H3117}.

translation_notes: אהל דם — 'Tent of Blood.' Acts 1:19 preserves the Aramaic name Ἁκελδαμάχ (חקל דמא, 'field of blood'), and the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'Chaqal Dema, that is, the field of the blood'; the Shem Tov ms's אהל ('tent') for חקל is a copyist's slip of one letter-group, itself evidence that the name came to this text in its Semitic form, not from Greek ἀγρὸς αἵματος.
עד היום הזה — the biblical narrator's formula (Gen 26:33; Josh 4:9).

verses.translation: Then{H227} was fulfilled{H7999} the word{H3982} of Zechariah{H2148} the prophet{H5030}: And I said to them: If it is good{H2896} in your eyes{H5869}, multiply{H7235} my wages{H7939}; and if not, forbear{H2308}. And they weighed{H8254} my wages{H7939}: thirty{H7970} pieces of silver{H3701}. And YHWH{H3068} said{H559} to me: Cast it{H7993} to the potter{H3335}. And this is from the man who forms{H3335} clay{H2789},

one_way_hebrew: The base text's רבו ('multiply my wages') differs by one letter from Zech 11:12's הבו ('give'); mss ABEF read הבו, matching the Masoretic text exactly — and mss ABEF likewise supply לא ('and if NOT'), and AEF read השליכהו, Zech 11:13's own form. The manuscript family carries the Masoretic wording of Zechariah within itself.
מאמר (H3982) — 'the word/decree' (Esth 1:15; 2:20; 9:32): late-biblical Hebrew, the register of this author.
greek_deviations: THE HEBREW NAMES ZECHARIAH. Greek Matthew attributes this prophecy to 'Jeremy the prophet' (Ἰερεμίου) — a difficulty commented on since Origen, for the quotation is Zech 11:12-13. The Shem Tov Hebrew reads אז נשלם מאמר זכריה הנביא, 'then was fulfilled the word of Zechariah the prophet,' and then quotes Zech 11:12-13 at length and nearly verbatim — 'If it is good in your eyes, [give] my wages; and if not, forbear. And they weighed my wages, thirty of silver. And YHWH said to me: Cast it to the potter' — where Greek Matthew gives only a loose two-verse summary. The Hebrew text quotes the right prophet in the prophet's own words; the Greek misnames him and paraphrases. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads Jeremiah with the Greek; Shem Tov stands with Zechariah.
textual_notes: ה״ — the ms writes ה״ ('The Name'), the scribal circumlocution for the Tetragrammaton; first occurrence in this chapter. Rendered YHWH.

Howard's apparatus (27:9): זכריה] omit G; להם] לכם A; רבו] הבו ABEF; ואם] + לא ABEF; ה״ אלי] omit G; השליכו] השליכהו AEF; היוצר¹] + אדם היקר אשר יקרתי מהם EF (completing Zech 11:13: 'the goodly price that I was prised at of them'); חרס] חרש BEFG; וזהו] וזה ABEG.

verses.translation: as my Lord{H136} commanded{H6680}.

one_way_hebrew: כאשר אדוני צוה — 'as my Lord commanded': the Torah's own compliance-formula (כאשר צוה יהוה, Exod 39-40 passim), sealing the Zechariah quotation the way Moses' narrative seals each fulfilled instruction.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} was standing{H5975} before{H6440} Pilat, and he asked{H7592} him: Are you the king{H4428} of the Jews{H3064}? And Yeshua{H3442} said{H559}: You say{H559} it.

one_way_hebrew: אתה אומר — the deflecting affirmation, third time in the Passion (26:25, 64): Hebrew court idiom, one voice across the three interrogations.

verses.translation: And when Yeshua{H3442} was pursued{H7291} by the great ones{H1419} of the priests{H3548} and the elders{H2205} of the people{H5971}, for any word{H1697} that they said{H559} against him he did not answer{H6030}.

one_way_hebrew: רודף — 'pursued, persecuted': Ps 119:161's exact scene — שרים רדפוני חנם, 'PRINCES have PERSECUTED me WITHOUT CAUSE' — and this text supplies all three members: the princes (v. 12), the pursuit (רודף), and the שנאת חנם, the causeless hatred (v. 18). The psalm of the persecuted Torah-keeper is the frame; Greek κατηγορεῖσθαι ('be accused') is courtroom procedure only.
translation_notes: רודף בעד — the participle is used passively ('pursued/harassed by'), late-Hebrew syntax; Howard renders 'was harassed by.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:12): בעד... העם] מגדולי העם הכהנים G.

verses.translation: And Pilat said{H559} to him: Do you not see{H7200} how many testimonies{H5715} there are against you?

translation_notes: עדיות — the mishnaic plural of עדות ('testimonies'; the tractate Eduyot bears the name): living rabbinic Hebrew from the narrator's own hand.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} him not a word{H1697}, and Pilat was exceedingly{H3966} amazed{H6381} at this.

one_way_hebrew: The threefold silence — before the priests (26:63), under their pursuit (27:12), and before Pilate (27:14) — is Isa 53:7 narrated: 'he was oppressed and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth.' The Hebrew Passion tells the Servant-song as event.

verses.translation: And on the honored{H3513} feast{H2282} day{H3117} of Pesach{H6453}, it was their custom that the official{H1489} of the city{H5892} give{H5414} to the people{H5971} one{H259} prisoner{H631} of the prisoners{H631} — the one whom they wished{H7521}.

translation_notes: מנהג — 'custom,' the rabbinic term (no biblical Strong's in this sense); another stroke of living Hebrew.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:15): החג] חג A; של פסח] שלהם EF; היה²] + לו AEFG.

verses.translation: And in the hand{H3027} of Pilat there was one bound{H2280} man who was almost{H4592} a madman; his name{H8034} was Barabbash. He had been taken{H3947} for murder{H7523}, and he had put him in the pit{H953}.

one_way_hebrew: בור — the pit of Joseph (Gen 37:24) and of Jeremiah (Jer 38:6), Hebrew narrative's own prison; and the exchange releases the guilty man from the בור while the innocent goes to the tree — the inversion a Hebrew reader feels in the word itself.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew draws Barabbas in three strokes the Greek lacks: he was 'ALMOST A MADMAN (כמעט שוטה),' he was 'taken FOR MURDER,' and he sat 'in the PIT (בור).' Greek Matthew has only δέσμιον ἐπίσημον, 'a notable prisoner.' The crowd's choice — the murderous madman from the pit over the righteous one — is far starker in the Hebrew telling.
translation_notes: שוטה — the rabbinic word for a madman (the halakhic category חרש שוטה וקטן); no biblical Strong's entry.
רצחה — late-Hebrew noun from רצח (H7523), the roots of לא תרצח (Exod 20:13).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:16): ברב״ש] ברבש EF, בראבאש A, בארבש B, ברבש G (spellings vary).
The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew calls him בר-אבן (Bar-Even, 'son of a stone'), another Hebrew guess at the name the Greek carries as Βαραββᾶς.

verses.translation: And when they were gathered{H622}, Pilat said{H559} to them: Which{H335} of these{H428} do you wish{H7521} that I release{H3240} — Barabbash, or Yeshua{H3442} who is called{H7121} Mashiach{H4899}?

translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads שנפרא; the scan of Howard's text reads שנקרא ('who is called'), corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:17): מאלו] + השנים A; שאניח] שתניחוני A.

verses.translation: This was because Pilat knew{H3045} that on account of baseless{H2600} hatred{H8135} he had been taken{H3947}.

one_way_hebrew: שנאת חנם — 'hatred without cause': the persecuted righteous man's own words in the Psalter — שנאי חנם, 'they that hate me without a cause' (Ps 69:5; 35:19), the psalms this Passion keeps touching (the gall and vinegar of Ps 69:22 come at vv. 34, 48). Greek Matthew reads διὰ φθόνον, 'for ENVY' — a different diagnosis. And שנאת חנם is the precise phrase the rabbis later made the cause of the Temple's destruction (b. Yoma 9b); the Hebrew Matthew hangs the verdict on the same words.

verses.translation: And while he was sitting{H3427} on the seat{H3678}, his wife{H802} sent{H7971} him a messenger, saying{H559}: I implore{H2470} you, in no matter{H6045} say a word{H1697} against{H5048} that righteous one{H6662}, for in this night{H3915} I have suffered{H5445} many{H7227} things in a vision{H4759} because of him{H1157}.

one_way_hebrew: סבלתי — 'I have BORNE/SUFFERED': סבל is Isa 53's carrying-verb (ומכאבינו סבלם, 'our pains — he bore them,' Isa 53:4; עונתם הוא יסבל, 53:11). In the Hebrew, the one Gentile voice for the צדיק speaks Isaiah's Servant-vocabulary of vicarious suffering — 'I have borne many things because of HIM.'
במראה — the מראה is biblical prophecy's own channel to those outside Israel (Gen 20:3-6, Abimelech; Gen 41, Pharaoh); Pilate's wife joins the line of warned Gentiles.
translation_notes: אחילה אני ממך — from the idiom חלה פנים, 'to entreat the face' (Exod 32:11); the wife's Hebrew is courtly.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads הילילה; the scan of Howard's text reads הלילה, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (27:19): אחילה] מחלה AEF, אחל G; צדיק] הצדיק BG; דבר] omit G.

verses.translation: And the great ones{H1419} of the priests{H3548} and the elders{H2205} of the law{H1881} assembled{H6950} the people{H5971}, that they should ask{H7592} for Barabbash and that Yeshua{H3442} be put to death{H4191}.

translation_notes: זקני הדת — 'the elders of the דת (law/religion),' with דת the Persian-period word of Esther (Esth 1:8) and Daniel: late-biblical Hebrew idiom for the religious establishment.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:20): הדת] העם B; ישאלו] שישאלו ABEF; ms A recasts the end: את ישו להמית ולא בראבאש ('to put Yeshua to death and not Barabbash').

verses.translation: And Pilat answered{H6030} them: Which{H335} of them do you wish{H7521} that we release{H3240}? And they said{H559}: Barabbash.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:21): Vs 21] omit EF; ms A omits איזה... ברבאש by haplography.

verses.translation: And Pilat said{H559} to them: If so, what{H4100} shall I do{H6213} with Yeshua{H3442} who is called{H7121} Mashiach{H4899}? And all of them answered{H6030}: Let him be hanged{H8518}.

one_way_hebrew: שיתלה — 'let him be HANGED' (תלה): the Hebrew tells the crucifixion throughout in the verb of Deut 21:22-23, כי יהיה באיש חטא משפט מות והומת ותלית אתו על עץ — 'hanged on a tree.' This is precisely the category in which Paul, a Hebrew reader, argues the cross (Gal 3:13, quoting 'cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree'). Greek σταυρωθήτω ('let him be crucified') is the Roman executioner's word; תלה is the Torah court's. A Hebrew author writes תלה natively; a back-translator from Greek σταυρόω, working mechanically, writes צלב (as the ר״ל gloss at v. 32 in fact does when explaining the object).
translation_notes: א״כ — the scribal abbreviation אם כן ('if so'), study-house shorthand in the narrative itself.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:22): ויאמר להם פילאט] omit A (haplography; see on vs 21); פילאט] omit G.

verses.translation: And Pilat said{H559} to them: What{H335} evil{H7451} has he done{H6213}? And they were crying out{H2199} with violence{H2394}: Hang him{H8518}! Hang him! Hang him!

greek_deviations: The cry is THREEFOLD: יתלוהו יתלוהו יתלוהו — 'hang him, hang him, hang him' — where Greek Matthew has the single σταυρωθήτω. The triple cry is Hebrew's own emphatic cadence — היכל יהוה היכל יהוה היכל יהוה (Jer 7:4), קדוש קדוש קדוש (Isa 6:3) — the mob chanting in the very rhythm of Hebrew liturgy. Mss BEF drop the third יתלוהו; the base text keeps all three.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:23): איזו רעה] מה A; יתלוהו³] omit BEF.

verses.translation: And Pilatus, when he saw{H7200} that there was no standing{H8617} and he was not able{H3201} to make peace{H7999} with them in any thing — before a great{H1419} quarrel should arise{H6965} among the people{H5971} because of this — took{H3947} water{H4325} and washed{H7364} his hands{H3027} before{H6440} the people{H5971} and said{H559}: I am innocent{H5355} of them; watch{H8104} yourselves what you do{H6213}.

one_way_hebrew: ורחץ ידיו... אני נקי — Pilate performs the Torah's own rite: Deut 21:6-7, where the elders nearest a slain man 'shall WASH THEIR HANDS... and shall answer and say, Our hands have not shed this blood' — the eglah arufah declaration of innocence from bloodshed, joined to the נקי of Deut 21:8-9 ('put away the guilt of INNOCENT BLOOD'). In Greek the hand-washing is an unexplained foreign gesture; in Hebrew it is a statute enacted — and Judas' confession (v. 4, דם נקי) and the people's answer (v. 25) complete the same Deut 21 frame.

תקומה (H8617) — 'no power to stand': the word occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, Lev 26:37 — the covenant-curse 'ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies.' The narrator spends this rare word on Pilate.
שמרו לכם — the Torah's warning formula (השמרו לכם, Exod 19:12; Deut 4:23).
translation_notes: קטטה — the rabbinic word for a quarrel (no biblical Strong's entry).
מהם — 'innocent of THEM'; mss ABEF read מהדם ('innocent of THE BLOOD'), and G מדם ישו ('of the blood of Yeshua'), as the Greek; Howard's English follows the variant: 'I am innocent (of the blood).'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:24): ופילאטוש] ופילאט AEFG; תקומה ולא] omit A; ולא יכול] ולא היה יכול EF; מהם] מהדם ABEF, מדם ישו G; לקח] + מעט A; שום] כל A; שמרו] למדו G.

verses.translation: And all{H3605} the people{H5971} answered{H6030} and said{H559}: His blood{H1818} will be upon us and upon our seed{H2233}.

one_way_hebrew: דמו עלינו — the biblical blood-guilt formula, self-invoked: 'his blood shall be upon his own head' (Josh 2:19); 'thy blood be upon thine own head' (2 Sam 1:16; 1 Kgs 2:32-33 — 'upon the head of Joab and upon the head of his SEED for ever'). The people answer Pilate's Deut 21 rite by taking upon themselves exactly what the rite disclaims — in the legal formula of their own Scriptures, with 1 Kgs 2:33's extension to the seed.
זרענו — 'our SEED,' the covenant word (Gen 12:7); Greek τέκνα ('children') is a household word, not a covenant one.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:25): וענו] והם ענו G; כל העם] כולם G; זרענו] זרעינו BEF.

verses.translation: And then{H227} he released{H3240} Barabbash to them, and delivered{H4560} to them Yeshua{H3442} — flogged and afflicted{H6031} — that they might hang him{H8518}.

one_way_hebrew: מעונה — 'AFFLICTED': the pual participle of ענה, precisely Isa 53:4's word — 'we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted (ומענה)' — with Isa 53:7 (נענה, 'he was afflicted') beside it. Greek φραγελλώσας reports a scourging; the Hebrew names the Servant. לקוי is the rabbinic flogging-word (מלקות), pairing the court's lash with the prophet's affliction in four Hebrew syllables.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק קי״ג (Perek 113) begins at the next verse.
Howard's apparatus (27:26): לה] להם AEF; ברבאש] ברבש A, בראבאש EF.

verses.translation: Then{H227} the horsemen{H6571} of the court{H2691} took{H3947} Yeshua{H3442} into custody{H4929} and assembled{H6950} before a great{H7227} congregation{H6951} of many peoples{H5971}.

one_way_hebrew: במשמר — 'in custody/under guard': Gen 40:3's word for Joseph's ward (במשמר בית שר הטבחים); the Joseph thread (sold by Judah/Yudah, put in the pit, held in custody) keeps surfacing in the Hebrew word-choices.
translation_notes: פרשי החצר — 'the horsemen of the court' (פרש, H6571), where Greek has 'the soldiers of the governor.'

verses.translation: And they clothed{H3847} Yeshua{H3442} with garments{H899} of silk{H4897} and wrapped{H5848} him in a green{H3387} silk{H4897} robe{H4598}.

one_way_hebrew: משי (H4897) occurs in the Hebrew Bible only in Ezek 16:10, 13 — YHWH clothing Jerusalem: 'I clothed thee also with embroidered work... I covered thee with SILK.' The mockers robe the king of Israel in the very fabric of Ezek 16's bridal clothing of Jerusalem — an irony that exists only in Hebrew, since Greek has no משי here.
מעיל (H4598) — the robe of kings and priests (1 Sam 18:4; Exod 28:31); the mockery uses the true regalia-word.
greek_deviations: A GREEN silk robe — Greek Matthew has a SCARLET cloak (χλαμύδα κοκκίνην; Mark and John, purple). The Hebrew tradition dresses the mock-king differently, and in משי — silk.

verses.translation: And they made{H6213} a crown{H5850} of thorns{H6975} and set it{H7760} on his head{H7218}, and put a reed{H7070} in his right{H3233} hand{H3027}, and kneeling{H3766} they were mocking{H3932} him: Shalom{H7965} upon you, king{H4428} of the Jews{H3064}!

one_way_hebrew: קוצים (H6975) — the thorns of the Adam-curse: וקוץ ודרדר תצמיח לך, 'thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee' (Gen 3:18). In Hebrew the crown of קוצים sets the ground's curse on the head of the man; Greek ἄκανθαι is botany without Genesis.
שלום עליך — the mock-homage borrows the true Hebrew royal greeting (cf. 26:49); Greek χαῖρε is the Roman ave.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:29): ביד] בידו G; אחת] אחד G; וישימהו] וישימו AEF; ממנו] + אומרים G.

verses.translation: And spitting{H7556} in his face{H6440}, they were taking{H3947} the reed{H7070} and striking{H5221} him on his head{H7218}.

one_way_hebrew: Isa 50:6 again supplies the map — 'I hid not my face from shame and from SPITTING (מכלמות ורק)' — with the smiting (מכים, H5221) of the same verse ('I gave my back to the SMITERS, למכים').
translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads יהיו; the scan of Howard's text reads והיו, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:30): ורוקקים] והיו רוקקים A.

verses.translation: And when they had mocked{H3932} him, they stripped{H6584} the robe{H4598} from him and clothed him{H3847} with his own clothing{H4403}, and gave orders{H6680} to hang him{H8518}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:31): מלבושו] מלבושיו ABEF.

verses.translation: And while they were going out{H3318} from the city{H5892}, they met{H6293} a man{H376} whose name{H8034} was Shimon{H8095} the Kena'ani{H3669}, and compelled him to carry the gallows — that is, the warp{H8359}-and-woof{H6154}.

one_way_hebrew: ר״ל השתי וערב — 'that is to say, the WARP-AND-WOOF': the text glosses צליבה with שתי וערב, the medieval-Hebrew household term for the cross-shape, drawn from the Torah's weaving vocabulary (שתי וערב, warp and woof, Lev 13:48-59). The gloss (ר״ל = רוצה לומר, 'it means to say') is written FOR Hebrew readers who know שתי וערב but need צליבה explained — the direction of explanation only makes sense in a Hebrew-reading community. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew uses שתי וערב outright for the cross throughout.

ואנסוהו — אנס, the rabbinic verb of compulsion (the halakhic אונס); Greek ἠγγάρευσαν is the Persian-loan 'impressed into service.' Each language reaches for its own legal loanword — the Hebrew's is rabbinic, not a calque.
greek_deviations: שמעון הכנעני — 'Shimon the KENA'ANI,' the same epithet Greek Matthew gives to Simon the Zealot (Matt 10:4, Σίμων ὁ Καναναῖος, from קנאי, 'zealot'); Greek Matthew here reads 'a man of CYRENE' (Κυρηναῖον). The Hebrew text either identifies the cross-bearer by the disciple's epithet or preserves the Semitic byname the Greek shifted to a place-name; the Vat. Ebr. 100 text reads 'a Qurini man, whose name was Shimon,' with the Greek.

verses.translation: And they came{H935} to a place{H4725} called{H7121} Gulgota, which is Mount{H2022} Calvari.

greek_deviations: הוא הר קאלווארי — 'that is, Mount CALVARY': the text glosses the Semitic place-name with the church's LATIN name (calvaria, 'skull'), exactly as it glossed בשורה with evangeli (24:14; 26:13) and the abomination with Antichristos (24:15). A Hebrew text annotated with the Latin vocabulary its readers heard from the church is a Hebrew text living among Latin-speaking Christians — not a fresh translation out of Greek, which has no 'Calvary' (Greek reads κρανίου τόπος, 'place of a skull').
translation_notes: למקים — so Howard's printed text (defective for למקום, 'to a place').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:33) records variant spellings of קאלווארי in mss A and EF.

verses.translation: And they gave{H5414} him wine{H3196} mixed{H4197} with gall{H4846}, and when he began{H2490} to drink{H8354} he perceived it and would not drink.

one_way_hebrew: The scene is Ps 69:22 — 'they gave me also GALL for my meat, and in my thirst they gave me VINEGAR to drink' — split across the crucifixion exactly as the psalm splits it: the gall in the wine here, the vinegar at v. 48. In the Hebrew both halves carry the psalm's own word-stock (מרה gall, חומץ vinegar); Greek χολή/ὄξος translates the same psalm at one remove.
translation_notes: מזוג — 'mixed' (from מזג; the noun in Song 7:3): the rabbinic term for diluted wine — living Hebrew usage.
הרגישו — late-Hebrew 'he sensed it' (no biblical Strong's in this sense).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:34): ירצה] רצה ABEF.

verses.translation: And afterward{H310}, when they had set him{H7760} on the gallows, they divided{H2505} his garment{H899} by lot{H1486}.

one_way_hebrew: חלקו בגדו בגורל — Ps 22:19 in its own verbs: יחלקו בגדי להם ועל לבושי יפילו גורל, 'they DIVIDED my garments among them, and upon my vesture they cast the LOT.' The narrative wears the psalm's consonants (חלק, בגד, גורל); Greek Matthew's διεμερίσαντο... βάλλοντες κλῆρον translates the same psalm, but only the Hebrew IS the psalm.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:35): בגדו] בגדיו ABEFG.

Greek 27:36 ('And sitting down they watched him there') has no counterpart in the Shem Tov text: Howard's apparatus reads 'Vs 36] omit all mss'; the text runs from v. 35 to v. 37. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew carries the verse ('And they sat, looking at him' — cf. Ps 22:18).

verses.translation: And afterward{H310} they placed{H3240} over his head{H7218} a writing{H4385} which said{H559}: This is Yeshua{H3442} of Nazrat, the king{H4428} of Israel{H3478}.

one_way_hebrew: מכתב (H4385) — 'a writing' (Exod 32:16, 'the writing of God'); the Hebrew uses the Torah's inscription-word for the titulus.
greek_deviations: מלך ישראל — the titulus reads 'the king of ISRAEL,' not 'king of the JEWS' (Greek: ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων). The Hebrew text keeps the covenant name — and it is consistent: the mockers at v. 42 say 'if he is the king of ISRAEL' in the Greek too, but only the Hebrew puts ישראל over his head. 'King of the Jews' is the outsiders' (Roman) formulation; 'king of Israel' is Israel's own — the title as a Hebrew community would write it.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:37): נאזרת] מנזראת EF; זה] זהו A; על ראשו מכתב אחד] 3 4 2 1 EF.

verses.translation: Then{H227} two{H8147} thieves{H1590} were hanged{H8518} with him, the one{H259} at his right{H3225} and the one at his left{H8040}.

one_way_hebrew: נתלו — 'were hanged' (תלה again); and גנבים — 'thieves' by the Torah's category (גנב, Exod 22:1), where Greek λῃσταί are brigands. The count-of-transgressors scene is Isa 53:12's ואת פשעים נמנה, 'he was numbered with the transgressors.'

verses.translation: And those passing by{H5674} were mocking{H3932} him and shaking{H5128} the head{H7218},

one_way_hebrew: מניעים ראש — Ps 22:8 verbatim: 'All they that see me laugh me to scorn (ילעגו — the very ילעיגו of this verse)... they SHAKE THE HEAD (יניעו ראש)'; cf. Lam 2:15. Both of the psalm's verbs — לעג and הניע ראש — stand here in the Hebrew text; Greek κινοῦντες τὰς κεφαλάς renders one of them.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:39): ראש] ראשם A.

verses.translation: and saying{H559}: See{H7200} — you who would lay waste{H2717} the Sanctuary{H4720} of El{H410} and in yet three{H7969} days{H3117} [restore it] — save{H3467} yourself{H6106}! If you are the Son{H1121} of El{H410}, come down{H3381} from the gallows.

one_way_hebrew: תושיע עצמך — 'SAVE yourself': the taunts of vv. 40-43 turn the root ישע over four times (תושיע, הושיע, להושיע, יושיעהו) — and ישע is the root of the name ישו״ע. In Hebrew every taunt unwittingly speaks his name; in Greek σῴζω has no echo of Ἰησοῦς.
translation_notes: The base text lacks 'build it'; ms A adds תבנהו ('you would build it'), which Howard's English follows: '(build it).'
Howard's printed text reads ראח, an evident printer's error for ראה (so the transcription's footnote 180).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:40): אפשר] איך A, אשר BEF; חרבת] אתה חרבת G; האל¹] אל F; ימים] + תבנהו A; מן הצליבה] מהצליבה EFG.

verses.translation: And the great ones{H1419} of the priests{H3548} and the elders{H2205} of the people{H5971} were mocking{H3932} him and saying{H559}:

greek_deviations: Greek Matthew adds 'with the scribes'; the Hebrew has priests and elders only.

verses.translation: The others{H312} he saved{H3467}; himself{H6106} he is not able{H3201} to save{H3467}. If he is the king{H4428} of Israel{H3478}, let him come down{H3381} from the tree{H6086}, and we will believe{H539}.

one_way_hebrew: מן העץ — 'let him come down from THE TREE': the Hebrew names the cross עץ, Deut 21:22-23's own noun (ותלית אתו על עץ... כי קללת אלהים תלוי) — the hanged man on the tree. Acts (5:30; 10:39) and Peter (1 Pet 2:24) preserve the same Hebrew idiom in Greek dress (ξύλον); this text has it natively.
הושיע... להושיע — the taunt's salvation-verbs speak the name ישו״ע (see v. 40); and מלך ישראל continues the titulus (v. 37).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:42): ונאמין] + בו ABG; האחרים הושיע] לאתרים רפא והושיע G.

verses.translation: For he leaned{H8172} on El{H410}; let him save him{H3467} now{H6258}, if he delights{H7521} in him — for he said{H559} that he is the Son{H1121} of Elohim{H430}.

one_way_hebrew: The mockery is Ps 22:9, and the Hebrew keeps the psalm's shape: 'he trusted on YHWH; let him deliver him... seeing he delighted in him (כי חפץ בו).' The Shem Tov's ירצה carries the psalm's delight-clause; and נשען ('leaned') is Isa 50:10's word for the Servant's posture — 'let him trust in the name of YHWH and LEAN (וישען) upon his God' — the mockers quoting the Servant-song against the Servant.
אלקים — the ms writes the reverent ק-spelling (first occurrence in this chapter); rendered Elohim.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:43): האלקים] האלים A; the בו added by ABG belongs to the end of v. 42 ('we will believe IN HIM').

verses.translation: And those same{H6106} words{H1697} the thieves{H1590} who were hanged{H8518} with him said{H559} to him.

textual_notes: The transcription's footnote 182 notes נתלים עמו stands in the wrong font in Howard's printed edition.

verses.translation: And at the sixth{H8345} hour{H8160}, darknesses{H2825} came over all the world{H5769} and remained{H5975} until the ninth{H8671} hour{H8160}.

greek_deviations: בכל העולם — 'in all the WORLD'; Greek ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν can be read 'over all the land.' The Hebrew is unambiguous and larger.
חשוכות — a plural, 'darknesses,' as if the plague-darkness of Exod 10:22 (חשך אפלה, a darkness that can be felt) came in waves.

verses.translation: Yeshua{H3442} cried{H6817} with a great{H1419} voice{H6963}, saying{H559} in the holy{H6944} tongue{H3956}: My El{H410}, my El{H410}, why{H4100} have you forsaken me{H5800}?

one_way_hebrew: THE CRY IS PS 22:2 IN THE PSALM'S OWN HEBREW — אלי אלי למה עזבתני — letter for letter the Masoretic consonants (עזבתני, 'you have forsaken me'). Greek Matthew must TRANSLITERATE the cry (ηλι ηλι λεμα σαβαχθανι — where σαβαχθανι is ARAMAIC שבקתני, not the psalm's Hebrew) and then translate it for its readers ('that is to say, My God, my God...'). The Hebrew Matthew needs no gloss: its readers hear the psalm directly. A text whose readers understand the cry unglossed is a text for Hebrew readers; the gloss-apparatus of the Greek is the mark of the translation.

בלשון הקודש — 'in the holy tongue': the narrator marks the dying cry as HEBREW (the rabbinic term לשון הקדש). Greek Matthew's Aramaic σαβαχθανι and this text's עזבתני cannot both be the sound from the cross; the Hebrew gospel claims the psalm was prayed as Scripture gives it — and the mishearing in v. 47 works best in exactly that case.
No variant is recorded in Howard's apparatus against עזבתני — the Shem Tov mss are unanimous in the psalm's Hebrew wording (letter-checked against the scan, Howard p. 146).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:46): יש״ו] ולשעה תשיעי׳ ישו A ('And at the ninth hour Yeshua cried...' — as Greek Matthew's 'about the ninth hour').

verses.translation: And one{H259} of those standing{H5975} there{H8033} said{H559}: This one is calling{H7121} for Eliyah{H452}.

one_way_hebrew: The mishearing is native to Hebrew: אֵלִי ('my El') is the first two syllables of אליה(ו). A bystander at a Hebrew cry mistakes אלי אלי for a call to Eliyahu naturally; a Greek reader needs the transliteration ηλι to see how the confusion arose. The pun that drives the scene lives in the Hebrew text and merely survives, embalmed, in the Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:47): לאליה] לאלוק EF ('calling to Eloah' — the EF scribes read the cry as addressed to God, not Elijah).

verses.translation: And immediately he took{H3947} a sponge and filled it{H4390} with vinegar{H2558} and gave{H5414} it to him to drink{H8354}.

one_way_hebrew: חומץ — 'VINEGAR': Ps 69:22's own word (ולצמאי ישקוני חמץ, 'in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink'), completing the psalm whose gall opened the scene (v. 34). The two Hebrew nouns of Ps 69:22 — gall and vinegar — bracket the crucifixion in this text's own vocabulary.
translation_notes: אספוג — the Greek loanword σπόγγος in rabbinic dress (m. Shabbat 21:3 ספוג); Howard renders 'spongy-bread.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:48): אספוג] הספוג EF.

verses.translation: And the others{H312} were saying{H559}: Let us see{H7200} if Eliyah{H452} will come{H935} and save him{H3467}.

one_way_hebrew: ויושיעהו — the salvation-root once more (see vv. 40, 42, 43): even the Elijah-watchers phrase their test in the consonants of his name.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} cried{H6817} another{H312} time{H6471} with a great{H1419} voice{H6963}, and sent{H7971} his breath{H5397} to his Father{H1}.

greek_deviations: ושלח נשמתו לאביו — 'he SENT his breath TO HIS FATHER': an act with a direction and an addressee. Greek Matthew has ἀφῆκεν τὸ πνεῦμα, 'he let go the spirit.' The Hebrew is Eccl 12:7 enacted — 'the breath returns to God who GAVE it' — with נשמה, the breath God breathed into the man (Gen 2:7), going home deliberately. The Vat. Ebr. 100 text reads 'sent Ruach Ha-Qodesh,' a different theology; Shem Tov's is the Preacher's.

verses.translation: And immediately the veil{H6532} of the Sanctuary{H4720} was torn{H7167} into two{H8147} pieces{H7168} from above{H4605} to below{H4295}, and the earth{H776} quaked{H7493}, and the stones{H68} were shattered{H7665}.

one_way_hebrew: פרכת (H6532) — the Torah's own word for the veil (Exod 26:31-33), which 'divides between the holy place and the most holy'; Greek καταπέτασμα translates it. A Hebrew author writes פרכת by instinct.

לשני קרעים — 'into two PIECES': קרעים is the noun of Ahijah's sign, the mantle torn to pieces (קרעים) to declare the kingdom torn from its king (1 Kgs 11:30-31), and of the mantle of Elijah's passing (2 Kgs 2:12). In Hebrew the Temple veil tears in the vocabulary of prophetic rending-signs.

verses.translation: And the graves{H6913} were opened{H6605}, and many{H7227} of the sleepers{H3463} of the dust{H6083} of the ground{H127} arose{H6965}.

one_way_hebrew: מישיני אדמת עפר — DAN 12:2 VERBATIM: ורבים מישני אדמת עפר יקיצו, 'and MANY OF THEM THAT SLEEP IN THE DUST OF THE GROUND shall awake.' The Hebrew Matthew narrates the resurrection of the saints in the resurrection-verse's own rare construct chain (three words that occur together nowhere else); Greek Matthew ('many bodies of the saints which slept arose') translates the idea and loses the quotation entirely. No back-translator from the Greek would land on Daniel's exact phrase.
והקברים נפתחו — and behind the opened graves, Ezek 37:12-13: 'I will OPEN YOUR GRAVES and cause you to come up out of your graves.' Two resurrection texts, both audible only in Hebrew.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:52): עפר] העפר B.

verses.translation: And they came out{H3318} from their graves{H6900}, and after{H310} they lived{H2421}, they entered{H935} the holy{H6944} city{H5892} and were revealed{H1540} to many{H7227}.

one_way_hebrew: עיר הקדש — 'the city of holiness': Isa 52:1's own title (עיר הקדש) in the verse that commands Jerusalem to awake and shake herself from the DUST — the chapter that opens the Servant-song this Passion has been quoting. The risen sleepers of the dust (v. 52) walk into Isa 52:1's dust-shaking city.

שחיו — 'they LIVED' (חיה): resurrection as living again (1 Kgs 17:22; Ezek 37:5 וחייתם), the same verb the priests quote at v. 63 (ויחיה) and the messenger uses at 28:6 (חי). One Hebrew verb carries the doctrine across the chapters.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:53): ונגלו] גלו EF; מקבורתם] מקברותם E.

verses.translation: And the captain{H8269} of the hundred{H3967} and those standing{H5975} with him to guard{H8104} Yeshua{H3442} saw the quaking{H7494} of the earth{H776} and the things that were done{H6213}, and they feared{H6342} exceedingly{H3966}, saying{H559}: In truth{H571}, this was the Son{H1121} of Eloah{H433}.

one_way_hebrew: שר המאה — 'the captain of the hundred': the Torah's own officer-title (שרי מאות, Exod 18:21; Num 31:14). Greek ἑκατόνταρχος is itself a calque of the Hebrew title; this text simply has the original.
translation_notes: האלוק — the ms writes Eloah with the reverent ק-substitution (אלוק for אלוה); rendered Eloah. Mss A and B spell it plainly, האלוה — the transcription's footnote 183 confirms ms A reads אלוה.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:54): האלוק] האלוה AB; ואומרים] ויאמרו AG, ואמר E; והדברים שנעשו] וכל הדברים אשר נעשו G.

verses.translation: And there were there{H8033} many{H7227} women{H802} standing{H5975} far off{H7350}, of those who served{H8120} Yeshua{H3442} from the Galil{H1551} until now{H3541}.

one_way_hebrew: עומדות מרחוק — 'standing FAR OFF': the sufferer's psalm again — 'my lovers and my friends stand aloof from my sore, and my kinsmen STAND AFAR OFF (מרחק עמדו)' (Ps 38:12; cf. Ps 88:9). The Hebrew scene keeps quoting the Psalter's map of abandonment.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:55): מאותן] מאותם G; כה] פה EF.

verses.translation: And among them was Maria Magdalena, and Miryam{H4813} the mother{H517} of Ya'aqov{H3290} and Yoseph{H3130}, and the mother{H517} of the sons{H1121} of Zavdel.

translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads אמ with a non-final mem; the scan reads אם, corrected here.
זבדאל — the El-form of Zebedee again (see 26:37).

verses.translation: And at the time{H6256} of evening{H6153} there came{H935} a rich{H6223} man{H120} from Karnasiah, whose name{H8034} was Yoseph{H3130}, and he was a disciple{H8527} of Yeshua{H3442}.

one_way_hebrew: אדם עשיר — 'a RICH man' receiving the body for burial: Isa 53:9, ואת עשיר במתיו — 'and with the RICH in his death.' The Hebrew noun עשיר is the Servant-song's own word; the narrative continues to be Isa 53 told as event (the affliction at v. 26, the silence at v. 14, the grave with the rich here).
translation_notes: מכרנאסיאה — a worn Hebrew spelling of Arimathea; the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads מהרמתים ('from Ramatayim' — 1 Sam 1:1's רמתים, Samuel's town), the transparent Hebrew form of the same name.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:57): שהיה מכרנאסיאה] omit G; the mss spell the town variously (A, EF).

verses.translation: And he went{H1980} to Pilat and asked{H7592} him for the body{H1480} of Yeshua{H3442}, and Pilat commanded{H6680} that it be given{H5414} to him.

translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads ופעלא״ט; the scan of Howard's text reads ופילא״ט, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:58): ושאל] לשאל B; הגוף] את הגוף A; מיש״ו] omit FG.

verses.translation: And Yoseph{H3130} took it{H3947} and wrapped it in a very costly{H2803} silk{H4897} garment{H899}.

greek_deviations: בבגד משי — a SILK garment again (see v. 28): Ezek 16:10's fabric (וׂאכסך משי, 'I covered thee with silk'). Greek has σινδόνι καθαρᾷ, 'clean linen,' and the Vat. Ebr. 100 text follows the Greek's linen; the Shem Tov burial is in the royal covering of Ezek 16 — YHWH's own clothing of Jerusalem wrapped around her king.
translation_notes: וכרכו — כרך, the rabbinic wrapping-verb (the tractate-word for wrapping scrolls and the dead); no biblical Strong's entry.

verses.translation: And he laid{H7760} him in his own tomb{H6913}, which was newly{H2319} hewn{H2672} from stone{H68}, and he laid{H7760} a great{H1419} stone{H68} over the mouth{H6310} of the tomb{H6913}.

one_way_hebrew: נחצב — the hewing-verb of Isa 22:16's rock-tomb (חצבי מרום קברו, 'thou hast hewed thee out a sepulchre on high') — and the burial completes Isa 53:9: with the rich man was his grave.
על פי הקבר — 'over the MOUTH of the tomb': the stone on the well's mouth (פי הבאר) that only the promised one rolls away (Gen 29:2-10) — Jacob at the well stands behind the Hebrew idiom.
textual_notes: Greek 27:61 ('And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre') has no counterpart in the Shem Tov text: Howard's apparatus reads 'Vs 61] omit all mss'; the text runs from v. 60 to v. 62. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew carries the verse.
Howard's apparatus (27:60): הקבר] omit G; פי] omit B.

verses.translation: And on the morrow{H4283} of the Pesach{H6453}, the great ones{H1419} of the priests{H3548} and the Perushim{H6567} came{H935} to Pilat,

one_way_hebrew: ממחרת הפסח — 'on the morrow of the Pesach': the Torah's own calendar phrase, verbatim (Num 33:3; Josh 5:11 — ממחרת הפסח). Greek Matthew writes a circumlocution — 'the next day, that followed the day of the PREPARATION (παρασκευή)' — dating by the Roman-Greek week; the Hebrew dates by Israel's festival calendar, and in doing so states plainly that the crucifixion day was the Pesach itself.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:62): הפסח] יום הפסח ABEF.

verses.translation: and they said{H559} to him: Our lord{H113}, we remember{H2142} that this liar{H8267} said{H559} while he was still in life{H2416} that at the end{H7093} of three{H7969} days{H3117} he will stand{H5975} and live{H2421}.

one_way_hebrew: שלקץ... יעמוד — 'at the END (קץ)... he will STAND (עמד)': Dan 12:13's resurrection idiom exactly — ותעמד לגרלך לקץ הימין, 'thou shalt STAND in thy lot at the END of the days.' Even his enemies quote him in Daniel's grammar of resurrection; the Hebrew resurrection-verb עמד runs from here through 28:6-8 (עמד, 'he arose'). Greek ἐγείρομαι ('be raised') is a different picture — lifting, not standing.
השקרן — 'this LIAR': the שקר root of 24:24's נביאי השקר; Greek πλάνος ('deceiver') answers to תעה, not שקר — the Hebrew charge is falsehood, the Greek's is misleading.
translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads השפרן; the scan of Howard's text reads השקרן, corrected here.

verses.translation: And therefore{H3651} command{H6680} that his tomb{H6913} be guarded{H8104} until the third{H7992} day{H3117}, for perhaps{H194} one of his disciples{H8527} will come{H935} and steal{H1589} him, and afterward{H310} they will say{H559} to the people{H5971} that he stood{H5975} from death{H4194}; and if they do{H6213} this, the last{H314} iniquity{H5771} will be greater{H1419} than the first{H7223}.

one_way_hebrew: שעמד מהמות — 'that he STOOD from death': the Hebrew resurrection-verb again (see v. 63); the priests' own mouths carry the chapter's resurrection grammar.
translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads ואם יעשו; the scan of Howard's text reads ואם זה יעשו, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:64): ולכן] ולכה B; האחרון] אחרון F.

verses.translation: And Pilat said{H559} to them: Seek out{H1245} guards{H8104}; guard{H8104} it the best{H3148} that you can{H3201}.

greek_deviations: בקשו שומרים — 'SEEK OUT guards': Pilate tells them to go find their own watch; Greek ἔχετε κουστωδίαν ('ye have a watch') hands them a Roman guard. In the Hebrew the tomb-watch is the priests' own arrangement from the start — which is why, at 28:11-15, the guards report to the priests and are paid by them, not by Rome.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (27:65): שמרו] ושמרו ABEFG.

verses.translation: And they completed{H7999} the structure{H1146} of the tomb{H6913} and sealed it{H2856}, and placed{H3240} guards{H8104} there{H8033}.

one_way_hebrew: וחתמוהו — 'and SEALED it': the sealed pit of the righteous man under royal watch is Daniel's den — 'a stone was brought and laid upon the mouth of the den, and the king SEALED it (וחתמה) with his own signet' (Dan 6:18) — and Daniel comes up alive at dawn. The Hebrew reader has seen this sealed stone before.
greek_deviations: שלמו בנין הקבר — 'they COMPLETED THE STRUCTURE of the tomb': the Hebrew has them finishing the tomb's masonry around the stone; Greek Matthew has them 'making the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone, and setting a watch.' Different pictures of the same precaution.
translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads והתמוהו; the scan of Howard's text reads וחתמוהו ('and sealed it'), corrected here.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 27 in the Shem Tov Hebrew is the crucifixion told in the Torah's legal categories and the Prophets' own consonants. (1) THE EXECUTION IS A HANGING: the crowd cries יתלוהו יתלוהו יתלוהו — 'hang him, hang him, hang him,' a threefold Hebrew cadence where Greek has one σταυρωθήτω (27:23; BEF drop the third cry); the verdict is שיתלה (27:22), the thieves 'were hanged' (27:38, 44), the taunt is 'come down from the TREE' (מן העץ, 27:42) — Deut 21:22-23's category throughout, the very ground of Gal 3:13; and Judas hangs himself (ותלה עצמו, 27:5) by the same verb. The cross itself is glossed in Hebrew for Hebrew readers: הצליבה ר״ל השתי וערב — 'the gallows, that is, the warp-and-woof' (27:32), the rabbinic term from Lev 13's weaving vocabulary; and Golgotha is glossed with church LATIN — 'that is, Mount Calvary' (27:33) — like evangeli and Antichristos before it. (2) THE QUOTATION IS ZECHARIAH'S, BY NAME: 27:9 reads 'then was fulfilled the word of ZECHARIAH the prophet' and quotes Zech 11:12-13 at length and nearly verbatim, where Greek Matthew says 'Jeremy' and paraphrases — the Hebrew names the right prophet (mss ABEF even carry the Masoretic הבו and השליכהו); the potter-of-clay wording (יוצר חרס, 27:7) touches Jer 19:1, showing how the Greek's Jeremiah arose. (3) PS 22 IN ITS OWN HEBREW: the cry from the cross is אלי אלי למה עזבתני 'in the holy tongue' (27:46) — the psalm's Masoretic consonants (עזבתני), NOT the Greek's transliterated Aramaic σαβαχθανι, and no Shem Tov ms varies; the Eliyah-mishearing (27:47) is a native Hebrew pun (אלי/אליה); the head-shaking of 27:39 is Ps 22:8's יניעו ראש; the garments divided בגורל (27:35) are Ps 22:19's verbs. Ps 69:22 frames the scene — gall in the wine (27:34), vinegar on the sponge (27:48). (4) ISA 53 AS EVENT: delivered 'flogged and AFFLICTED' (מעונה = Isa 53:4's word, 27:26); the threefold silence (26:63; 27:12, 14 — Isa 53:7); Pilate's wife 'SUFFERED (סבלתי) many things for him' (27:19 — Isa 53:4's verb); the RICH man's tomb (עשיר, 27:57 — Isa 53:9). (5) DEUT 21 ENACTED: Judas confesses shedding דם נקי (27:4 — Deut 27:25's curse); Pilate washes his hands declaring innocence (27:24 — the eglah arufah rite of Deut 21:6-8, with Lev 26:37's hapax תקומה); the people answer in the blood-formula of Josh 2:19/1 Kgs 2:33 — 'his blood upon us and upon our SEED' (27:25). (6) THE RESURRECTION TEXTS: 27:52 quotes Dan 12:2 verbatim — רבים מישיני אדמת עפר קמו, 'many of the sleepers of the dust of the ground arose' (invisible in Greek); the priests quote the promise in Dan 12:13's idiom — 'at the END he will STAND and LIVE' (27:63-64); the sealed stone under guard is Dan 6:18's den (27:66). (7) Distinctive readings: Barabbas is 'almost a MADMAN,' held 'in the PIT' for murder (27:16); Pilate knows the motive is שנאת חנם, 'BASELESS HATRED' (27:18 — Ps 69:5; Greek: 'envy'); the mock-robe is GREEN silk (27:28, Greek scarlet) and the shroud silk too (27:59, Greek linen) — משי, Ezek 16:10's fabric; the titulus reads 'king of ISRAEL' (27:37, Greek 'king of the Jews'); the darkness covers 'all the WORLD' (27:45); he 'SENT his breath to his Father' (27:50 — Eccl 12:7); the burial dates 'on the MORROW OF THE PESACH' (27:62 — Num 33:3's phrase, where Greek has 'after the preparation-day'); Pilate says 'SEEK OUT guards' (27:65 — the watch is the priests' own). The salvation-taunts of 27:40-49 turn the root ישע — his own name — four times. Judas returns the coins 'in TESHUVAH' (27:3) and the blood-money pun דמי דם (27:6) works only in Hebrew. Verses 36 and 61 are absent from all Shem Tov mss (both present in Vat. Ebr. 100). ה״ ('The Name') stands at 27:9-10; the reverent spellings אלקים (27:43) and אלוק (27:54; AB read אלוה) mark the divine names. Shem Tov's section headings fall at vv. 1 (Perek 112) and 27 (113).
